你现在继续开发「戏境 AI」项目。

你的身份：

高级AI应用工程师
+
Multi-Agent系统工程师
+
3D数字资产工程师
+
比赛项目技术负责人


当前任务：

执行 Phase 4 检查点A。

注意：

当前阶段只允许：

代码审查
+
架构分析
+
技术方案设计


禁止：

修改代码

安装依赖

调用Neural4D API

调用任何付费API

创建新的功能文件


完成方案后必须停止，等待用户批准。


==================================================
一、项目背景
==================================================


项目名称：

戏境 AI


项目定位：

基于京剧非遗知识库、多Agent协作和AI数字资产生成的文化IP智能创作平台。


当前目标：

将京剧文化知识、AI Agent创作流程和3D数字资产生成结合，形成完整的非遗数字IP生产流程。


==================================================
二、当前项目完成情况
==================================================


Phase 1：

已完成：

- 京剧文化展示网站
- AI戏韵工坊
- HTML/CSS/JavaScript前端架构
- AI能力展示模块


Phase 2：

已完成：

- FastAPI后端
- 京剧私有RAG知识库
- SQLite知识管理
- Qdrant向量数据库
- BGE中文Embedding
- DeepSeek真实调用
- 引用追踪


Phase 3：

已完成：

- Multi-Agent工作流
- Planner Agent
- Research Agent
- Designer Agent
- Culture Reviewer Agent
- 角色设计JSON输出
- 人工确认流程


当前Agent流程：

用户需求

↓

Planner Agent

↓

Research Agent

↓

京剧RAG知识库

↓

Designer Agent

↓

Culture Reviewer Agent

↓

Character JSON


Phase 4目标：

将Character JSON转化为：

可展示、可交互的京剧数字3D IP资产。


==================================================
三、Phase 4核心目标
==================================================


实现：

京剧数字IP生成中心。


完整流程：


用户需求

↓

Multi-Agent创作

↓

角色设计JSON

↓

视觉Prompt

↓

角色概念图

↓

Neural4D图生3D

↓

Web 3D Viewer展示

↓

企业应用展示



最终展示目标：

评委可以看到：

AI如何从京剧文化知识开始，

经过多个Agent协作，

最终生成一个可以自由查看的3D数字角色。


==================================================
四、最高优先级限制：Neural4D API调用次数
==================================================


整个项目Neural4D真实API调用：

最多：

3次。


包括：

- 测试
- 调试
- Demo生成


全部计算。


禁止：

❌ 自动循环调用

❌ 前端无限生成

❌ 每次Prompt修改重新调用

❌ Agent自动触发Neural4D


必须采用：


Mock流程验证

↓

人工确认Prompt

↓

少量真实调用



==================================================
五、Neural4D调用规划
==================================================


第一次：

技术验证。


目的：

验证：

- API连接
- 输入格式
- 输出格式
- 模型文件是否可加载


不是最终展示。


第二次：

比赛核心模型。


必须经过：

Planner

↓

Research

↓

Designer

↓

Reviewer


生成最终Prompt。


第三次：

企业模式展示模型。


用于：

游戏公司IP

或者

地方文旅IP。



==================================================
六、当前执行任务：Phase 4检查点A
==================================================


现在不要开发。


先执行：


1.

检查当前Git状态。


确认：

Phase 3成果完整。


检查：

git status

git branch

git log



2.

检查项目结构。


重点：

backend/

agents/

frontend/

js/

css/

docs/


3.

检查Phase 3输出。


确认：

Character JSON是否适合作为3D生成输入。


4.

检查当前AI戏韵工坊页面。


分析：

如何加入：

数字IP生成中心。


5.

检查是否已有：

模型展示能力。


==================================================
七、生成架构方案文档
==================================================


创建：

docs/reports/phase-04-neural4d-architecture-proposal.md



必须包含：



# 1. Phase 4目标


说明：

如何完成：

文化知识

↓

AI创作

↓

3D数字资产



---

# 2. 总体技术架构


设计：


Phase 3 Character JSON

↓

Visual Prompt Generator

↓

Image Asset

↓

Neural4D

↓

3D Model Storage

↓

Web Viewer



---

# 3. Neural4D服务设计


说明：

- API调用方式
- 输入要求
- 输出格式
- 文件保存方式
- 错误处理


---

# 4. Neural4D额度保护设计


必须设计：

Neural4D Quota Manager


示例：


{
used_calls:0,
max_calls:3,
remaining_calls:3
}



每次调用前：

必须检查额度。



超过限制：

拒绝调用。


---

# 5. 3D Viewer技术方案


必须重点设计。


比较：

方案A：

Three.js


方案B：

model-viewer


方案C：

其他Web 3D方案



分析：

- 开发成本
- 浏览器兼容
- GLB支持
- 比赛展示效果


最终选择。


---

# 6. 3D交互硬性要求


必须满足：


网页端3D模型展示必须支持：

## 鼠标交互

包括：

- 鼠标拖拽旋转
- 左右旋转查看
- 连续观察模型


## 触摸交互

包括：

- 手机触摸拖动
- 双指缩放


## 缩放

支持：

- 放大
- 缩小


## 旋转范围


必须支持：

至少260°连续拖拽观察。


最佳实现：

360°水平旋转能力。


禁止：

- 静态图片
- 视频旋转
- GIF


---

# 7. 3D Viewer状态设计


必须设计：


Loading状态：

例如：

正在加载京剧数字角色模型...



Ready状态：

模型加载完成。



Error状态：

例如：

模型加载失败，请检查资源。



不能出现：

空白区域

无提示失败。


---

# 8. 3D模型格式设计


优先：

GLB / GLTF


说明：

- 文件管理
- 加载方式
- 浏览器兼容


必须设计：

模型资源检查流程。


---

# 9. 前端展示设计


新增：

AI数字IP生成中心。


展示：


区域1：

Agent创作过程


Planner

↓

Research

↓

Designer

↓

Reviewer



区域2：

角色方案


区域3：

3D Viewer


区域4：

企业模式入口



---

# 10. 企业模式设计


增加：


个人模式：

京剧文化体验


企业模式：

游戏公司

文旅机构

IP设计服务



流程：


企业需求

↓

Agent团队

↓

文化研究

↓

角色设计

↓

3D数字资产



---

# 11. Phase 4测试计划


必须包含：


## API测试

- Neural4D额度控制
- 请求错误
- 文件返回


## 3D测试

必须测试：


- 模型加载成功
- GLB完整
- 鼠标拖拽旋转
- 至少260°观察范围
- 触摸旋转
- 缩放
- Loading显示
- Error显示


## 浏览器测试

测试：

Chrome

手机浏览器

桌面端


---

# 12. Git计划


创建：

feature/phase4-neural4d



提交规划：


feat: add character asset schema

feat: add visual prompt generator

feat: add neural4d service layer

feat: add quota protection

feat: add 3d viewer

feat: add enterprise mode

test: add phase4 tests

docs: add phase4 report



---

# 13. Prompt记录计划


保存：

docs/prompts/phase-04/


包括：

- 3D生成Prompt
- 角色Prompt
- API调用决策
- 失败案例
- 优化过程



==================================================
八、Phase 4开发阶段（批准后执行）
==================================================


收到：

“Phase 4检查点A批准，开始开发。”


之后才能执行。


开发顺序：


Step 1：

建立Character Asset Schema。


Step 2：

建立Visual Prompt Generator。


Step 3：

建立Neural4D Service。


Step 4：

建立Quota Manager。


Step 5：

建立Mock 3D流程。


Step 6：

第一次Neural4D调用。


Step 7：

建立3D Viewer。


Step 8：

第二次Neural4D生成比赛模型。


Step 9：

企业模式。


Step 10：

第三次Neural4D生成商业展示模型。



==================================================
九、最终验收标准
==================================================


Phase 4必须满足：


[ ] Phase 3 JSON正确复用

[ ] Visual Prompt生成

[ ] Neural4D服务封装

[ ] API调用≤3次

[ ] 调用记录完整

[ ] Quota保护有效

[ ] 3D模型网页展示

[ ] 鼠标拖拽旋转

[ ] 手机触摸旋转

[ ] 至少260°连续拖拽观察

[ ] 缩放功能

[ ] Loading状态

[ ] Error失败状态

[ ] GLB/GLTF支持

[ ] 3D Viewer测试完成

[ ] 企业模式完成

[ ] Git记录完整

[ ] Prompt记录完整

[ ] 阶段报告完成



==================================================
十、停止规则
==================================================


现在：

只执行Phase 4检查点A。


输出：

docs/reports/phase-04-neural4d-architecture-proposal.md


完成后：

立即停止。


等待用户回复：


“Phase 4检查点A批准，开始开发。”
我会先核对 Phase 3 的代码、Git记录和角色JSON，再查阅 Neural4D 与网页3D查看器的官方资料。本次只生成架构方案文档，不改功能代码、不安装依赖、不调用付费API。

#### Staging & Camera Control. Use these features to frame the perfect shot for your model

## Use the camera-controls attribute to enable user interaction
    
    `<model-viewer camera-controls touch-action="pan-y" src="../../shared-assets/models/Astronaut.glb" alt="A 3D model of an astronaut"></model-viewer>`

## Set the camera-orbit change the initial angle and position of the camera
    
    `<model-viewer camera-controls touch-action="pan-y" camera-orbit="45deg 55deg 4m" src="../../shared-assets/models/Astronaut.glb" alt="A 3D model of an astronaut"></model-viewer>`

## Use CSS-like calc() to sync camera orbit with scroll position
    
    `<model-viewer camera-controls touch-action="pan-y" camera-orbit="calc(-1.5rad + env(window-scroll-y) * 4rad) calc(0deg + env(window-scroll-y) * 180deg) calc(5m - env(window-scroll-y) * 10m)" src="../../shared-assets/models/Astronaut.glb" alt="A 3D model of an astronaut"></model-viewer>`

## The camera automatically interpolates between orbits (even when controls are disabled)
    
    `<model-viewer id="orbit-demo" interpolation-decay="200" src="../../shared-assets/models/Astronaut.glb" alt="A 3D model of an astronaut"></model-viewer>
    <script>
    (() => {
      const modelViewer = document.querySelector('#orbit-demo');
      const orbitCycle = [
        '45deg 55deg 4m',
        '-60deg 110deg 2m',
        modelViewer.cameraOrbit
      ];
    
      setInterval(() => {
        const currentOrbitIndex = orbitCycle.indexOf(modelViewer.cameraOrbit);
        modelViewer.cameraOrbit =
            orbitCycle[(currentOrbitIndex + 1) % orbitCycle.length];
      }, 3000);

## By default, the camera targets the center of the model's bounding box
    
    `<model-viewer camera-controls touch-action="pan-y" auto-rotate src="../../shared-assets/models/odd-shape-labeled.glb" alt="An abstract 3D model with labeled origin and center" shadow-intensity="1" ar></model-viewer>`

## Use the camera-target attribute to orbit a different coordinate
    
    `<model-viewer camera-controls touch-action="pan-y" camera-target="0m 0m 0m" auto-rotate src="../../shared-assets/models/odd-shape-labeled.glb" alt="An abstract 3D model with labeled origin and center" shadow-intensity="1" ar></model-viewer>`

## Disable Tap

Pan is enabled by default via two fingers on touch or using right-click or any modifier key with mouse drag. When panning, the center point is shown visually (and can be suppressed/changed using the pan-target slot) and when the pan gesture ends, the camera is focused on that model point (if there was a surface under the dot), so that the camera doesn't orbit around a random point in space. Clicking on the model focuses on that point, while clicking off the model returns to the default center.

There is a disable-pan attribute to turn all of this off, but here we demonstrate only turning off the click/tap behaviors via the disable-tap attribute. Note that after panning and rotating the model, it can be very hard to get back to the original centering, so it's recommended to implement your own re-centering logic via camera-target if you decide to go this route.

-Infinity 0deg auto  | $theta $phi $radius

#### max-field-of-view

Set the maximum field of view of the camera, corresponding to maximum zoom-out. Takes values in the same form as field-of-view, but does not support env(). The default "auto" is the same as the default field-of-view.

#### inputSensitivity

Multiplier for all user inputs: mouse, touch, and keyboard. Allows for selectively fine control or to make custom interaction prompts move the model less compared to the fingers.

### Methods

#### resetTurntableRotation(theta)

Resets the turntable that rotates the model when auto-rotate is enabled. The new value of the turntable rotation will be theta radians after this method is invoked, but the model may not update until the next render frame. If no argument is supplied, theta defaults to zero.

#### resetInteractionPrompt()

Typically, the interaction prompt will only display once and then stops displaying after the user interacts with the 3D model for the first time. You can invoke this method in order to reset the interaction prompt after it has already been displayed. Doing so will cause it to display once again when the interaction-prompt display conditions have been met.

#### getCameraOrbit()

Returns the realtime orbital position of the camera. The returned object has theta, phi, and radius properties along with a toString() method suitable for putting in the camera-orbit attribute. Azimuthal (theta) and polar (phi) angles are represented as radians, and the distance (radius) is represented in meters. This value may differ from the value configured with the camera-orbit attribute on account of user interaction or camera interpolation.

# How to use the Image to 3D feature?

Last updated: September 2026 7 min read

Image to 3D turns a reference image into a 3D model. This guide covers input preparation, topology and texture settings, generation time, inspection, and download.

## Step 1: Open Image to 3D

Go directly to the Image to 3D Studio, or open Neural4D Studio and select Image to 3D.

## Step 2: Prepare and upload your image

You can click, drag, or paste an image into the upload area. Supported formats are PNG, JPG, JPEG, and WebP. The maximum file size is 20 MB.

Use an image with  | Avoid
--- | ---
One clear subject that is fully visible  | Multiple disconnected objects or a cropped subject
A plain background that contrasts with the subject  | A background with similar colors or a busy scene
Even lighting and visible edges  | Strong shadows, glare, or heavy reflections
An opaque object with a readable silhouette  | Glass, transparent surfaces, or motion blur

A front or three-quarter view usually gives the model enough visual information to form a clear silhouette. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# GLTFLoader

A loader for the glTF 2.0 format.

glTF (GL Transmission Format) is an open format specification whenever possible. Be advised that image bitmaps are not automatically GC-collected when they are no longer referenced, and they require special handling during the disposal process.

`GLTFLoader` supports the following glTF 2.0 extensions:

  * KHR_draco_mesh_compression
  * KHR_lights_punctual
  * KHR_materials_anisotropy
  * KHR_materials_clearcoat
  * KHR_materials_dispersion
  * KHR_materials_emissive_strength
  * KHR_materials_ior
  * KHR_materials_specular
  * KHR_materials_transmission
  * KHR_materials_iridescence
  * KHR_materials_unlit
  * KHR_materials_volume
  * KHR_mesh_quantization
  * KHR_meshopt_compression
  * KHR_texture_basisu
  * KHR_texture_transform
  * EXT_materials_bump
  * EXT_meshopt_compression
  * EXT_mesh_gpu_instancing

# OrbitControls

Orbit controls allow the camera to orbit around a target.

OrbitControls performs orbiting, dollying (zooming), and panning. Unlike TrackballControls, it maintains the "up" direction `object.up` (+Y by default).

## Code Example
    
    `const controls = new OrbitControls( camera, renderer.domElement );
    // controls.update() must be called after any manual changes to the camera's transform
    camera.position.set( 0, 20, 100 );
    controls.update();
    function animate() {
    	// required if controls.enableDamping or controls.autoRotate are set to true
    	controls.update();
    	renderer.render( scene, camera );
    }
    `

## Import

OrbitControls is an addon, and must be imported explicitly, see Installation#Addons.
    
    `import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';`

L30: 
L31: Last updated: September 2026 7 min read
L32: 
L33: cite8†Image to 3D turns a reference image into a 3D model. This guide covers input preparation, topology and texture settings, generation time, inspection, and download.
L34: 
L35: ## Step 1: Open Image to 3D
L36: 
L37: Go directly to the cite3†Image to 3D Studio , or open Neural4D Studio and select Image to 3D.
L38: ## Step 2: Prepare and upload your image
L39: 
L40: You can click, drag, or paste an image into the upload area. Supported formats are PNG, JPG, JPEG, and WebP. The maximum file size is 20 MB.
L41: Use an image with  | Avoid
L42: --- | ---
L43: One clear subject that is fully visible  | Multiple disconnected objects or a cropped subject
L44: A plain background that contrasts with the subject  | A background with similar colors or a busy scene
L45: Even lighting and visible edges  | Strong shadows, glare, or heavy reflections
L46: An opaque object with a readable silhouette  | Glass, transparent surfaces, or motion blur
L47: A front or three-quarter view usually gives the model enough visual information to form a clear silhouette. If exact geometry on several sides matters, use the available multi-view workflow instead of combining several objects into one image.
L48: 
L49: cite28†Image: Examples of suitable reference images for Image to 3D L50: ## Step 3: Choose topology, polycount, and materials
L51: 
L52: Choose the settings that match your next step before you submit the task.
L53: Setting  | Options  | When to use it
L54: --- | --- | ---
L55: Topology  | Triangle or Quad. Triangle is selected by default.  | Triangle preserves more surface detail. Quad is useful when you plan further editing or animation work.
L56: Polycount  | Triangle: 100,000 to 500,000. Quad: 1,000 to 100,000. The default is 50,000.  | Use a higher value for more detail and a lower value for a lighter model.
L57: Texture  | Optional  | Adds the model's visible surface color.
L58: PBR  | Optional  | Adds PBR material maps for physically based rendering workflows.
L59: Pose  | Auto, A-Pose, or T-Pose. Auto is selected by default.  | A-Pose and T-Pose are subscription features for humanoid characters intended for rigging or animation.
L60: Each selected option is charged separately. A Quad base mesh costs 15 Credits, Texture costs an additional 10 Credits, and PBR costs an additional 10 Credits. Quad with both Texture and PBR costs 35 Credits in total.
L61: 
L62: cite29†Image: Topology, polycount, Texture, and PBR settings in Image to 3D L63: ## Step 4: Generate and inspect the model
L64: 
L65: Click Generate. An untextured base mesh takes about 90 seconds. Texture and PBR generation are separate processing steps and take additional time, so a complete textured model normally takes more than two minutes.
L66: 
L67: When the result opens, rotate and zoom around it. Check the silhouette, thin parts, hidden sides, holes, and texture alignment. If the result does not match the reference, adjust the input or settings and submit a new generation.
L68: A regular Image to 3D result cannot be transferred to Neural4D-2o for conversational editing. Neural4D-2o can edit only a model generated inside its current session.
L69: 
L70: cite30†Image: Inspecting an Image to 3D result in Neural4D Studio L71: ## Step 5: Download or continue your workflow
L72: 
L73: Click the Download icon and choose GLB, OBJ, FBX, USDZ, STL, or BLEND. Quad models support all six formats. OBJ is only the default selection in the Quad download dialog.
L74: 
L75: Your generated files remain available in the cite31†Assets Library . For a physical version, use the available One-Click Make option on the generated model.
L76: 
L77: cite32†Image: Download options for an Image to 3D model L78: ## Frequently asked questions
L79: 
L80: Why did I get a white model?
L81: If Texture was not selected, the expected result is an untextured base mesh. If you selected Texture and the completed asset is still white, reload the saved asset and follow the cite33†generation error guide .
L82: 
L83: Can I edit this model in Neural4D-2o?
L84: No. Neural4D-2o edits only models generated in the current Neural4D-2o session.
L85: 
L86: Which format should I download?
L87: See cite34†the Neural4D format guide for common uses of each format.
L88: No reference image? Start with cite35†Text to 3D .

L51: Text to 3D API: The Backend for Infinite Asset Generation
L52: 
L53: Quick Summary
L54: 
L55: A Text to 3D API turns text prompts into production-ready 3D models through an asynchronous generate-and-poll workflow.
L56:   * Generation is asynchronous: submit a prompt, receive a UUID, and poll until the model URL is ready.
L57:   * Output formats include .glb, .fbx, .obj, .stl, .usdz, and .blend for Unity, Unreal Engine, and Three.js.
L58:   * The Neural4D text to 3D API costs 60 Power credits per generation, roughly $0.15 at paid-plan credit rates.
L59:   * Neural4D combines text, image, and multi-view inputs with watertight, manifold-closed output geometry.
L60: Developers building asset pipelines for games, UGC platforms, or procedural environments use a text to 3D API to replace stored asset files with generated ones. The Neural4D text to 3D API exposes one async workflow: submit a prompt, poll with the returned UUID, and download the finished model. Endpoints, credit costs, status codes, and geometry guarantees determine whether that output is engine-ready.

L73: Most game engines today still operate on a file retrieval mindset.
L74: 
L75: A designer defines a level.
L76: 
L77: Artists manually create props.
L78: 
L79: Developers import fixed files into the build. The result is predictable. Every player sees the same crate, the same barrel, the same bench.

L81: A generative pipeline works differently.

L83: Instead of storing assets, the system stores intent.

L120: ## Part 2: How the Neural4D Text to 3D API Works
L121: 
L122: High-fidelity 3D generation is computationally expensive. It cannot be treated as a synchronous request.
L123: 
L124: Neural4D’s API is designed to be asynchronous by default.
L125: A generation request returns a set of UUIDs rather than blocking the connection. You keep the UUID, poll the `retrieveModel` endpoint, and download the finished model once the job reports completion. The official cite34†Neural4D API quickstart†docs.neural4d.com walks through this request and poll flow with examples in cURL, Python, Node.js, Go, and Java.
L126: This architecture allows developers to trigger hundreds of generation requests without overwhelming their infrastructure. A forest, city block, or dungeon can be generated in parallel, with assets arriving as they are ready.
L127: The output formats include .glb, .fbx, .obj, .stl, .usdz, and .blend, making the API compatible with Unity, Unreal Engine, and web-based 3D frameworks such as Three.js. Format conversion runs through a dedicated `convertToFormat` endpoint, and a `queryJobProgress` endpoint exposes progress for monitoring long-running batches.
L128: 
L129: For teams building automated pipelines, this asynchronous design is essential.
L130: ### Text, Image, and Multi-View Input Modes
L131: 
L132: The API does not have to be text-only. The Neural4D API exposes the same asynchronous workflow across three input modes, each billed in Power credits:
L133:   * Text to 3D (`generateModelWithText`, 60 credits): the core path covered here, taking a prompt string and returning model UUIDs.
L134:   * Image to 3D (`mattingImage` followed by `generateModelWithImage`, 80 credits): mat an image first, then generate from the matted result to preserve a specific silhouette or concept across a batch.
L135:   * Chibi character models (`createCuteModelsFromImages`, 30 credits): stylized cute characters from uploaded images, useful for avatars and UGC content.
L136: All three modes reuse the same `retrieveModel` polling flow, so one integration pattern covers the entire API surface.

L143:     import time
L144: 
L145:     API_KEY = "your_token_here"
L146:     BASE_URL = "https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api"
L147: 
L148:     headers = {

L154:     resp = requests.post(
L155:         f"{BASE_URL}/generateModelWithText",

L157:         headers=headers,

L160: 
L161:     # 2. Poll until the model is ready

L164:             f"{BASE_URL}/retrieveModel",

L168:         code_status = result.get("codeStatus")

if key in public_fields} for row in rows]}\r\n\r\n    @app.post('/api/v1/chat', response_model=QuestionAnswer)\r\n    async def chat(data: QuestionRequest, request: Request):\r\n        key = request.headers.get('X-Idempotency-Key')\r\n        if key and (len(key) > 128 or not all(c.isalnum() or c in '-_' for c in key)):\r\n            raise ServiceError('INVALID_IDEMPOTENCY_KEY', '请求标识格式不正确。', 400)\r\n        signature = hashlib.sha256(data.model_dump_json().encode()).hexdigest()\r\n        now = time.monotonic()\r\n        for old in list(cache):\r\n            if now - cache[old][2] > 600: cache.pop(old)\r\n        if key and key in cache:\r\n            if cache[key][0] != signature: raise ServiceError('IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT', '同一请求标识不能用于不同问题。', 409)\r\n            return cache[key][1]\r\n        if key and key in pending:\r\n            raise ServiceError('REQUEST_IN_PROGRESS', '该问题正在处理，请等待当前回答。', 409, True)\r\n        if len(pending) >= 2: raise ServiceError('CHAT_BUSY', '问答正在处理其他请求，请稍后重试。', 429, True)\r\n        slot = key or str(uuid.uuid4())\r\n        pending[slot] = signature\r\n        try:\r\n            async with asyncio.timeout(settings.request_timeout_seconds):\r\n                retrieval = await runtime.knowledge(lambda: runtime.search_service.search(data.question, settings.retrieval_top_k, None, settings.retrieval_mode))\r\n                answer = await grounded_answer(data.question, retrieval, runtime.provider, request.state.request_id)\r\n            if key:\r\n                cache[key] = (signature, answer, time.monotonic())\r\n                while len(cache) > 128: cache.popitem(last=False)\r\n            return answer\r\n        except TimeoutError:\r\n            raise ServiceError('REQUEST_TIMEOUT', '本次问答超时，未自动重发模型请求；请稍后重试。', 504, True)\r\n        finally: pending.pop(slot, None)\r\n\r\n    register_agents(app, supervisor)\r\n\r\n    @app.get('/{path:path}')\r\n    async def frontend(path: str):\r\n        if path == 'favicon.ico': return Response(status_code=204)\r\n        return public_file(path)\r\n    return app\r\n\r\napp = create_app()\r\n"}

L103: The 3D Asset Delivery Format
L104: 
L105: glTF™ is a royalty-free specification for the efficient transmission and loading of 3D scenes and models by engines and applications. glTF minimizes the size of 3D assets, and the runtime processing needed to unpack and use them. glTF defines an extensible publishing format that streamlines authoring workflows by enabling the interoperable use of 3D content across the industry.

L111: ### glTF: The JPEG of 3D
L112: 
L113: * * *
L114: 
L115: The core of glTF is a JSON file that describes the structure and composition of a scene containing 3D models, which can be stored in a single binary glTF file (.glb). The top-level elements of the file include: Scenes and nodes, cameras, meshes, buffers, materials, textures, skins and animations.
L116: 
L117: In 2022 glTF 2.0 was released as the cite95†ISO/IEC 12113:2022 International standard , recognizing glTF's global position as a 3D asset format.

L184: ## Khronos PBR (Physically Based Rendering)
L185: 
L186: * * *
L187: Khronos glTF PBR defines a set of parameters that are used within glTF to simulate real-world lighting interactions, materials, and surface properties. The combination of glTF’s efficient delivery and PBR’s realism has become a game-changer for the 3D industry, empowering artists and developers to deliver compelling and visually captivating experiences.
L188: A wide range of physical properties are supported, with detailed descriptions available in the core glTF 2.0 specification and accompanying material Extensions.
L189: cite131†Image L190: #### glTF PBR Properties
L191: 
L192: The following glossary showcases some of the material effects that form part of the official Khronos PBR specification.
L193: 
L194:   * Alpha Coverage
L195:   * Ambient Occlusion
L196:   * Base Color
L197:   * Emissive & Emissive Strength
L198:   * Metallic
L199:   * Normal
L200:   * Roughness
L201:   * Anisotropy
L202:   * Clearcoat
L203: 
L204:   * Dispersion
L205:   * Index of Refraction
L206:   * Iridescence
L207:   * Sheen
L208:   * Specular
L209:   * Transmission
L210:   * Volume
L211:   * and more ...
L212:

L215: cite133†Image: Image Background L216: The Portable GPU Friendly Texture Format
L217: ## KTX 2.0 - Delivering GPU Compressed Textures in glTF
L218: 
L219: * * *
L220: KTX (Khronos Texture) is an efficient, lightweight container format supported by glTF for reliably distributing GPU textures to a diverse range of platforms to reduce asset file size and GPU memory usage. KTX adds the ability to specify textures using KTX v2 images with Basis Universal supercompression and is available in viewers and applications supporting the cite134†KHR_texture_basisu†github.com extension.
L221: The contents of a KTX file can range from a simple base-level 2D texture to a cubemap array texture with mipmaps. A wide range of open-source tools are available to help artists and developers create, convert, validate and transcode KTX compressed textures.
L222: cite13†Learn More L223: 
L224: RENDER EVERYTHING, EVERYWHERE
L225: ## glTF and 3D Commerce
L226: 
L227: * * *
L228: The Khronos 3D Commerce Working Group brings together industry-leading e-commerce companies to remove the barriers to deploying 3D commerce at scale using glTF. The group helps drive the development of the glTF format and ecosystem to meet the needs of 3D commerce including creating 3D authoring guidelines, tutorials and tools.
L229: Projects have included the development of the Material Variants extension and the glTF Asset Auditor and glTF Validator tools for streamlining and validating asset creation pipelines.

L236: TRUE-TO-LIFE 3D COLOR RENDERING
L237: ## Khronos PBR Neutral Tone Mapper
L238: 
L239: * * *
L240: 
L241: The Khronos PBR Neutral Tone Mapper enables faithful reproduction of a product’s base color, hue and saturation when using PBR rendering under grayscale lighting, while eliminating HDR artifacts around highlights. It has been designed to display 3D assets rendered using PBR with true-to-life colors that are vital in eCommerce, architecture and CAD, and is enjoying wide adoption by 3D tools and engines
L242:

The element will call your `load` method when it would normally load a glTF, lazily by default. Make sure to set the `src` to something (any string will do) to indicate this is not an empty element. Make sure to call our `progressCallback` occasionally, which will update our progress bar, and ensure you set a progress value of 1.0 when your pixels are ready to be shown. You must return us a `FramingInfo` object containing two numbers: `framedRadius` and `fieldOfViewAspect` to allow our camera to set its defaults. The `framedRadius` is the size of the bounding sphere and `fieldOfViewAspect` is the ideal element aspect ratio to frame the model (1.0 is a good default).
We will call your `render` method when the camera changes and pass you the `Camera` object containing `viewMatrix: Array<number>` and `projectionMatrix: Array<number>` as 4x4 matrices. Use this to update the rendered pixels in your canvas slot element. We will call your `resize` method when the element is resized so you can take coordinated action on your slotted canvas element.

#### unregisterRenderer()

Switches back to default rendering of a glTF/GLB src and stops calling any external renderer. Note you must manually remove your own slotted canvas element concurrently.

### Static Methods

#### mapURLs(callback)

If provided, the callback will be passed each resource URL before a request is sent. The callback may return the original URL, or a new URL to override loading behavior. This behavior can be used to load assets from .ZIP files, drag-and-drop APIs, and Data URIs.

Additional delay from the "load" event can be caused by the renderer compiling its shaders.

#### model-visibility

This event is fired when the visibility of the model changes. When the model is loaded, the element is in the viewport (assuming there is an IntersectionObserver), this event will fire and event.detail.visible will be "true".

#### progress

This event fires while a model, environment, skybox, variant, and/or a usdz conversion is loading, during both download and processing. The progress of all of these concurrent tasks will be given by a value between 0 and 1: event.detail.totalProgress. It also provides the reason why the event is fired ('model-load', 'environment-update', 'variant-update', 'usdz-conversion'): event.detail.reason.

#### render-scale

This event fires when the element is attached to the DOM and whenever the rendered DPR (device pixel ratio) changes, which is generally due to our renderer scaling its resolution to maintain frame rate. The event.detail contains the reportedDpr (window.devicePixelRatio), our renderedDpr (<= reportedDpr), minimumDpr (based on minimumRenderScale), reason ('GPU throttling' or 'No meta viewport tag'), and pixelWidth/pixelHeight (rendered resolution of the element). #### updateFraming()

Recalculates the camera defaults in case the model has been changed, for instance by the orientation or scale attributes.

updateFraming example

#### getMinimumFieldOfView()

Returns the minimum camera vertical field of view in degrees.

#### getMaximumFieldOfView()

Returns the maximum camera vertical field of view in degrees.

#### getIdealAspect()

Returns the ideal aspect ratio for the poster image for this model as currently framed.

#### zoom(keyPresses)

Applies the default zoom behavior (a combination of radius and field of view change), mimicking keyboard or mouse wheel inputs. If keyPresses = 1.0, it will zoom in as much as a single keystroke; negative values zoom out.

#### interact(duration, finger0, finger1)

Creates a synthetic touch interaction, ideal for creating custom interaction prompts. The duration (ms) and finger0 are required, while finger1 is optional and will create zoom/pan interactions instead of rotation if specified. Any other camera change will automatically cancel this motion and interact() cannot be called while a current synthetic interaction is playing. Each finger input is an object with x and y members, each of which has initialValue and keyframes members. The keyframes are an array of objects with frames and value members. The values are between 0 and 1, spanning the width/height of the element. The frames are a relative unit of time, where their sum is normalized to the duration. Each frame eases in and out between values. Visualize the touch points using the finger0/finger1 slots.

customPrompt example

### Events

#### camera-change

Fired when the camera position and/or field of view have changed. If the change occurred due to user interaction, the event.detail.source property will be set to "user-interaction". For the interaction-prompt or the interact() method, it will be set to "automatic". For other API camera changes, it is set to "none".

#### interact-stopped

Fired when the interact() motion stops. You can tell it completed by checking that event.detail.source is set to "automatic", while it was canceled early if the source is "user-interaction" or "none" (for JS camera changes).

### Slots

#### interaction-prompt

By placing a child element under <model-viewer> with slot="interaction-prompt", this element will replace the default hand icon which wiggles back and forth with the model until the user interacts.

#### finger0/finger1

Use in combination with interact() to specify an HTML element to represent each moving touch point. By placing a child element under <model-viewer> with slot="finger0", this element will appear and move along the path specified in the finger0 input of the interact() method, and similarly for finger1. Empty by default.

customPrompt example

#### pan-target

By placing a child element under <model-viewer> with slot="pan-target", this element will replace the small default circle that appears when the user is panning to indicate the camera's target.

# Function attachControl

  * attachControl(
    camera: ArcRotateCamera,
    canvas: HTMLCanvasElement,
    scene?: SceneContext,
    options?: AttachControlOptions,
): () => void

Attach orbit/zoom/pan controls to an ArcRotateCamera. Matches Babylon.js ArcRotateCameraPointersInput behavior with inertia:

    * Primary-button drag: rotate (alpha/beta) with momentum by default
    * Secondary-button drag: pan (shift target) with momentum by default
    * Wheel: zoom (radius) with momentum
    * Pinch: zoom (touch, direct — no inertia)

Mouse and pen button actions can be configured independently through AttachControlOptions.pointerMappings. Touch and wheel behavior are fixed so remapping desktop pointer buttons cannot alter mobile gestures. Keyboard input is a separate opt-in installed by enableArcRotateKeyboardControls; mappings and sensitivities are configured through AttachControlOptions.keyboard.

Input handlers accumulate into the camera's inertial offset properties. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Customizing Camera Inputs

### Table Of Contents

> Note: This page covers the legacy plugin-style input manager (`camera.inputs`). It currently applies to `FreeCamera`, `UniversalCamera`, `FollowCamera`, `FlyCamera`, and the VR / touch-joystick inputs — but those cameras are being ported to the newer declarative inputMap + movement system used by `ArcRotateCamera` and `GeospatialCamera` today, documented in Camera Movement and Input System. For the cameras already on the new system, existing legacy flags (e.g. `useCtrlForPanning`, `panningMouseButton`, `useAltToZoom`, `inertia`, `panningInertia`) continue to work and are bridged onto the new inputMap automatically — but new customizations should prefer the new system.
## Configure your inputs

Most inputs provide settings to customize the sensibility and adapt it to your own scene.

Each input provides a short name available on the manager. The goal is to provide a friendly syntax when playing with your inputs.

[Button: ES6][Button: ES6 pure][Button: UMD]
    
    `
    
    import { FreeCamera } from "@babylonjs/core/Cameras/freeCamera";
    
    import { FreeCameraGamepadInput } from "@babylonjs/core/Cameras/Inputs/freeCameraGamepadInput";
    
    import { Vector3 } from "@babylonjs/core/Maths/math.vector";
    
    const camera = new FreeCamera("sceneCamera", new Vector3(0, 1, -15), scene);
    
    camera.inputs.add(new FreeCameraGamepadInput());
    
    camera.inputs.attached.gamepad.gamepadAngularSensibility = 250;
    
    `

## Adding an existing input

The input managers of `ArcRotateCamera` and `FreeCamera` expose short-hand functions for adding built-in inputs.

    import { FreeCamera } from "@babylonjs/core/Cameras/freeCamera";
## HammerJS Input

If the built-in touch controls for the ArcRotateCamera are not enough for you, you can implement your own camera input using the well-known touch gesture library HammerJS: https://hammerjs.github.io/

We have an example of how to use HammerJS to simulate something similar to Google Earth controls. We use BabylonJS's ArcRotateCamera for this purpose. The camera is locked on the Y axis, horizontal pan moves the camera along the X axis, and vertical pan moves it along the Z axis. The camera's `alpha` angle is taken into account when panning. By pinching, you can change the camera's `radius` to zoom in and out. You can change the camera's `alpha` angle with a two-finger rotate gesture, so you can rotate around the camera's target.

Example app: https://demos.babylonjs.xyz/hammerjs-example/#/

GitHub repo: https://github.com/RolandCsibrei/babylonjs-hammerjs-arc-rotate-camera

The example contains `utils\ArcRotateCameraHammerJsInput.ts`, which implements `ICameraInput<ArcRotateCamera>`. There are multiple parameters for the input, and they are pretty self-explanatory. Please refer to the input source code and set the sensitivity and threshold values that fit your needs. First, you need to install HammerJS. Please refer to https://hammerjs.github.io/getting-started/ and import it.
    
    `
    
    import "hammerjs";
    
    `

To use the new input, add it to your `camera.inputs` after you have created the camera. To avoid one input fighting the other, remove `ArcRotateCameraPointersInput` from `camera.inputs`. After you create your input, you can set its parameters. The default values (please refer to https://github.com/RolandCsibrei/babylonjs-hammerjs-arc-rotate-camera/blob/680cf12155924a818faac5ff9d7f0a0271bb632b/src/utils/ArcRotateCameraHammerJsInput.ts#L21) are good for a general touch-screen monitor, so you may need to adjust them for your needs.
    
    `
    
    // remove mouse input
    
    camera.inputs.removeByType("ArcRotateCameraPointersInput");
    
    
    
    
    // add hammer js input
    
    const hammerJsInput = new ArcRotateCameraHammerJsInput();
    
    // now you can set the parameters you like
    
    // let's double the zoomSensitivity (default is 1)
    
    hammerJsInput.zoomSensitivity = 2;
    
    // add the input to the camera
    
    camera.inputs.add(hammerJsInput);
    
    `

Feel free to use this input class as a starter for your own HammerJS-based input.

On top of that, event handling is taken care of for you. While there is less flexibility in going this route, it might be easier to work with.

# Interface ArcRotateCamera

ArcRotateCamera — orbits around a target point. Uses Babylon.js convention: left-handed, alpha=rotation around Y, beta=elevation. Plain data + methods. Does NOT know about the scene.

Push-based dirty tracking: alpha/beta/radius use Object.defineProperty, target uses ObservableVec3. Changes call wm.markLocalDirty() immediately.

Inertia follows the Babylon.js model: input handlers accumulate per-frame offsets (inertialAlphaOffset, etc.) which are applied and exponentially decayed each frame by the controls module.

# Interface Camera

Minimal camera contract — any camera that can provide view/projection matrices. Both ArcRotateCamera and FreeCamera implement this interface. Pure state, no scene knowledge (pillar 4b).

# Function setCameraLimits

  * setCameraLimits(
    camera: ArcRotateCamera,
    limits: ArcRotateCameraLimits,
    scene?: SceneContext,
): () => void

Configure orbit/zoom limits on an ArcRotateCamera. This is fully opt-in and self-contained: cameras that never call it pay zero cost and bundle no clamping code (the camera's scalar setters call an undefined hook).

What it does:

    1. Stores the provided bounds on the camera and clamps the current pose into range right away (inertia zeroed), so enabling limits never causes a jump.
    2. Installs a self-clamp hook on the camera (`_clampToLimits`). The alpha/beta/radius setters invoke it on every mutation, so any caller — pinch direct-write, inertial overshoot, auto-rotate — is snapped back to the wall in the same statement that pushed past it. The camera is therefore never observably out of bounds at any point a per-frame callback reads it (e.g. a camera-pinned skybox), eliminating both the overshoot-then-snap jiggle and the one-frame clip "blink" of a deferred per-frame clamp.

Only the fields present on `limits` are written, so calls compose; pass a field as `undefined` to remove that bound. Returns a disposer that removes the self-clamp hook.

The optional `scene` parameter is accepted for backward compatibility and is unused — enforcement no longer needs a per-frame scene hook.

#### Parameters

    * camera: ArcRotateCamera
    * limits: ArcRotateCameraLimits
    * `Optional`scene: SceneContext

L16: #### Image generation
L17: 
L18: - [Create image generation tasks](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/v1-api-reference/image-generation/create-image-generation-tasks.md): Creates asynchronous image generation tasks from a prompt and optional image references supplied by file ID or HTTPS URL.
L19: #### Video generation
L20: 
L21: - [Create video generation tasks](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/v1-api-reference/video-generation/create-video-generation-tasks.md): Creates asynchronous video generation tasks from a prompt and optional frame or reference assets supplied by file ID or HTTPS URL.
L22: #### Tasks
L23: 
L24: - [Retrieve a task](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/v1-api-reference/tasks/retrieve-a-task.md): Returns task status and output by batch task ID or child image or video UUID. Provide exactly one of the id or uuid query parameters.

L32: ### API reference
L33: #### Text to 3D
L34: 
L35: - [Generate model from text](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/text-to-3d/generate-model-from-text.md): Generate 3D models from a text prompt. Supports model count, mesh quality, target face count, and mesh-only output. Existing defaults are preserved when the new options are omitted.
L36: #### Model management
L37: - [Retrieve model](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/model-management/retrieve-model.md): Retrieve a generated model by UUID.
L38: - [Convert model format](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/model-management/convert-model-format.md): Convert a generated model into a target format and return the download URL. This operation consumes 10 points.
L39: - [Query job progress](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/model-management/query-job-progress.md): Query the current progress of a model generation job by UUID.
L40: #### Image to 3D
L41: - [Generate model with image](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/image-to-3d/generate-model-with-image.md): Generate 3D models from one uploaded image. Supports model count, mesh quality, target face count, and mesh-only output. Existing defaults are preserved when the new options are omitted.
L42: - [Generate chibi-style model with image](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/image-to-3d/generate-chibi-style-model-with-image.md): Generate chibi-style 3D character models from uploaded images and a configured style tag. This operation consumes 30 points. The style tag must be configured in advance.
L43: #### Picture and video generation
L44: - [Generate picture](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/media-generation/generate-picture.md): Generate images from a text prompt with optional reference images. You can upload up to 6 reference images and submit 1 to 4 generation jobs in a single request.
L45: - [Generate video](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/media-generation/generate-video.md): Generate videos from a text prompt with optional reference images. You can upload 0 to 6 reference images and submit 1 to 4 generation jobs in a single request.
L46: - [Retrieve generation result](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/media-generation/retrieve-generation-result.md): Query the generation result by UUID. This is a query-only operation and does not consume points.

L48: 
L49: - [Detect portrait image](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/account-and-validation/detect-portrait-image.md): Check whether an uploaded image contains a human portrait.
L50: - [Query remaining balance](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/account-and-validation/query-remaining-balance.md): Query the remaining points balance available for later operations.

# Python AI 3D Model Generator API: Batch Game Assets with Code

Python AI 3D Model Generator API: Batch Game Assets with Code

Quick Summary

  * This guide shows how to batch generate hundreds of game-ready 3D assets with code, driving the Neural4D API from a single Python script.
  * Direct3D-S2 and Single Surface Approximation (SSA) deliver watertight, manifold-closed meshes with no manual retopology needed.
  * The async request-poll pattern used by all major AI 3D APIs works identically with Neural4D, taking about 90 seconds per untextured base mesh or 2+ minutes when full PBR textures are generated in the same job.
  * Commercial rights are included with paid plans, and text to 3D generation costs 60 Power credits per call, making large-scale asset production viable for indie studios.
  * Output formats (.glb, .fbx, .obj, .stl, .usdz, .blend) are ready for direct import into Unity, Unreal Engine, or web viewers.
## Part 2: API Setup: Authentication, Python Environment, and Endpoints

Neural4D’s API quickstart uses Bearer Token authentication, and the full reference is in the API documentation. You generate a token from your dashboard, set it as an environment variable, and every POST request carries it in the Authorization header. The API accepts both text prompts and image uploads, making it a flexible AI 3D model generator endpoint for any batch workflow.

The Python dependencies are minimal: the standard library `urllib` or the third-party `requests` package. No GPU is required since all inference runs on Neural4D’s cloud infrastructure.
    
    `import os

    BASE_URL = "https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api"
    GENERATE_URL = f"{BASE_URL}/generateModelWithText"
    RETRIEVE_URL = f"{BASE_URL}/retrieveModel"
    
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json"
    }
    `

Create an isolated virtual environment for your pipeline to avoid dependency conflicts across projects. The script runs on any machine with Python 3.8 or later.

### API Endpoint Reference

All Neural4D capabilities live under one REST base URL, `https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api`, and every endpoint uses Bearer Token authentication with a POST request. The submit-then-poll lifecycle matches the pattern established by the SDKs that dominate this search space: the tripo3d PyPI package exposes task submission, waiting, and balance checks, and the Meshy API documentation covers the same task queue and polling model. Developers who have integrated either SDK will find the Neural4D contract familiar.

Endpoint  | Method  | Purpose
--- | --- | ---
`generateModelWithText`  | POST  | Generate a model from a text prompt
`generateModelWithImage`  | POST  | Generate a model from a matted reference image
`mattingImage`  | POST  | Remove the background from an uploaded image before generation
`createCuteModelsFromImages`  | POST  | Generate a stylized (chibi) character model from an image
`retrieveModel`  | POST  | Poll a task and fetch the finished model by UUID
`convertToFormat`  | POST  | Re-export a model to fbx, glb, obj, stl, blend, or usdz
`queryJobProgress`  | POST  | Query the progress of a running generation job
`queryPointsInfo`  | POST  | Query the remaining credit balance
`checkHumanImage`  | POST  | Detect whether an uploaded image contains a human portrait

Charged calls consume 60 credits for `generateModelWithText`, 80 for `generateModelWithImage`, 30 for `createCuteModelsFromImages`, and 10 for `convertToFormat`. Status and balance queries such as `retrieveModel`, `queryJobProgress`, and `queryPointsInfo` consume no credits, so polling is always free.

## Part 3: Building the Batch Generation Loop

All major AI 3D generation APIs follow the same async pattern: you submit a task, poll for completion, and download the result. Neural4D’s API works identically across both its Text to 3D API and Image to 3D endpoints, so if you have used any other AI 3D model generator API before, the integration pattern is familiar.

### Single Asset Generation Function

The core function submits a text or image prompt and waits for the result. Generation time varies by texture setting: about 90 seconds for the base mesh, then 2 minutes or more when PBR textures (Normal, Roughness, Metallic maps) are generated in the same job. The mesh is produced first, and textures are applied as a follow-on pass, so a fully textured model takes longer than the untextured base mesh.

> The official API documentation describes the timing as “about 90 seconds per untextured base mesh,” with PBR texture generation extending the same job by several minutes.
    
    `def generate_3d_asset(prompt, textures=False):
This is where using Neural4D as your AI 3D model generator pays off: the loop keeps running until every asset is generated, no manual restart needed between items.
    
    `import csv
    
    prompts = []
    with open("asset_prompts.csv") as f:
        reader = csv.DictReader(f)
        for row in reader:
            prompts.append(row)
    
    for item in prompts:
        url = generate_3d_asset(item["prompt"])
        filename = f"output/{item['id']}_{item['name']}.glb"
        with open(filename, "wb") as f:
            f.write(requests.get(url).content)
        print(f"Downloaded {filename}")

Running this against a list of fifty prompts produces fifty ready-to-import `.glb` files with no manual intervention. For long-running batches you can poll `queryJobProgress` with the same UUID to track generation progress, and call `convertToFormat` after `retrieveModel` succeeds to export as `fbx`, `obj`, `stl`, `blend`, or `usdz` in addition to the default GLB. The Image to 3D model endpoint accepts a reference image URL alongside the text prompt, which helps maintain visual consistency across a batch of related assets. For a deeper look at why this matters for production workflows, see why your next project needs an Image to 3D API.

### Code Status and Error Handling Reference

Every `retrieveModel` response returns a `codeStatus` integer that tells you exactly where a task stands. Handling all five states inside the batch loop keeps a long-running job from dying silently on the first failed asset.

codeStatus  | Meaning  | What to do
--- | --- | ---
0  | Generation complete  | Download `modelUrl` and move to the next asset
1  | Generating in progress  | Keep polling on the same UUID
-1  | Token invalid or expired  | Regenerate the API key and restart the batch
-2  | UUID does not exist  | Re-submit the generation request
-3  | Generation failed  | Read `message`, adjust the prompt, and retry

Format conversion adds its own state via `statusType`: 0 means the converted model is ready to download, 1 means conversion is still running (poll again in a few seconds), and -1 means the request parameters are incorrect or the conversion failed, so retry with a valid `modelType` such as `fbx`, `obj`, or `stl`. The same `statusType` convention signals whether a `queryJobProgress` or `queryPointsInfo` query itself was valid.


### Rate Limits and Concurrent Requests

The Neural4D API is asynchronous: each `generateModelWithText` call returns a UUID immediately and generation runs server-side, so a long request never blocks your script. For a first batch, submit assets in small groups and collect the returned UUIDs before polling, rather than launching one thread per prompt. A concurrency factor of 2 to 4 works reliably for most pipelines; if the API returns a throttling error such as `429`, apply exponential backoff starting at 5 seconds and doubling the delay on each retry. This pacing pattern is the same one the SDKs in this space document: Meshy routes batch creation through a task queue, and Tripo exposes an async context manager, both of which prefer paced submission over unbounded parallel calls.

### Scope Limitations

Neural4D's 3D generation pipeline works on models it generates itself. It cannot import, retopologize, or repair meshes created by other tools. If you need to clean up a third-party model, the best strategy is to generate a fresh version with a corrected prompt rather than attempting post-hoc fixes. Before choosing any AI 3D model generator, confirm that its output format matches your engine's import pipeline.

### Textures in the Same Job, No Second Request

Unlike some competitors that require a separate API call to add textures after the mesh is confirmed, Neural4D keeps the whole job in one request. The base mesh generates first, then the PBR maps are applied in the same job, so you submit once and poll until the fully textured model is ready. This eliminates the risk of misalignment between geometry and its material layers and keeps the batch pipeline linear rather than branching.

For additional guidance on prompt structure, see the best practices for AI image to 3D model prompts. Teams using OpenClaw for pipeline orchestration can reference the OpenClaw Neural4D 3D Model API guide for framework-specific integration patterns.


Q: How does Neural4D compare to Meshy or Tripo for game assets?

Neural4D's Direct3D-S2 architecture with Spatial Sparse Attention produces watertight, manifold-closed meshes that go directly into a game engine. Meshy and Tripo use probabilistic generation that frequently outputs non-manifold geometry (unclosed surfaces, internal faces) requiring manual repair. Neural4D also applies PBR textures within the same generation job, whereas some competitors require a separate texture generation step after the mesh is confirmed. For batch generation at scale, a reliable AI 3D model generator like Neural4D dramatically reduces post-processing overhead.

Q: Can I use my own reference images for batch generation?

Yes, the Image to 3D API endpoint accepts a reference image URL alongside the text prompt. Passing your own concept art or reference photos as input helps the model match a specific style or silhouette across the entire batch. Use consistent lighting and composition in your reference images for the most uniform results.

# Text to 3D API for Programmatic 3D Asset Generation | Neural4D

Text to 3D API: The Backend for Infinite Asset Generation

Quick Summary

A Text to 3D API turns text prompts into production-ready 3D models through an asynchronous generate-and-poll workflow.

  * Generation is asynchronous: submit a prompt, receive a UUID, and poll until the model URL is ready.
  * Output formats include .glb, .fbx, .obj, .stl, .usdz, and .blend for Unity, Unreal Engine, and Three.js.
  * The Neural4D text to 3D API costs 60 Power credits per generation, roughly $0.15 at paid-plan credit rates.
  * Neural4D combines text, image, and multi-view inputs with watertight, manifold-closed output geometry.

Developers building asset pipelines for games, UGC platforms, or procedural environments use a text to 3D API to replace stored asset files with generated ones. The Neural4D text to 3D API exposes one async workflow: submit a prompt, poll with the returned UUID, and download the finished model. Endpoints, credit costs, status codes, and geometry guarantees determine whether that output is engine-ready.

## Part 1: From Static Assets to Generative Pipelines

Most game engines today still operate on a file retrieval mindset.

A designer defines a level.

Artists manually create props.

Developers import fixed files into the build. The result is predictable. Every player sees the same crate, the same barrel, the same bench.

A generative pipeline works differently.

Instead of storing assets, the system stores intent.

A level script can describe what it needs using text strings such as “rusty oil barrel”, “wooden supply crate”, or “alien artifact with glowing seams”. These descriptors are sent to a scalable generation endpoint, which produces unique assets on demand.

The asset library no longer exists as a folder. It exists as code potential.

This approach is fundamentally different from reconstructing a specific object from a reference image, which is better handled by an Image to 3D API.
## Part 2: How the Neural4D Text to 3D API Works

High-fidelity 3D generation is computationally expensive. It cannot be treated as a synchronous request.

Neural4D’s API is designed to be asynchronous by default.

A generation request returns a set of UUIDs rather than blocking the connection. You keep the UUID, poll the `retrieveModel` endpoint, and download the finished model once the job reports completion. The official Neural4D API quickstart walks through this request and poll flow with examples in cURL, Python, Node.js, Go, and Java.

This architecture allows developers to trigger hundreds of generation requests without overwhelming their infrastructure. A forest, city block, or dungeon can be generated in parallel, with assets arriving as they are ready.

The output formats include .glb, .fbx, .obj, .stl, .usdz, and .blend, making the API compatible with Unity, Unreal Engine, and web-based 3D frameworks such as Three.js. Format conversion runs through a dedicated `convertToFormat` endpoint, and a `queryJobProgress` endpoint exposes progress for monitoring long-running batches.

For teams building automated pipelines, this asynchronous design is essential.

### Text, Image, and Multi-View Input Modes

The API does not have to be text-only. The Neural4D API exposes the same asynchronous workflow across three input modes, each billed in Power credits:

  * Text to 3D (`generateModelWithText`, 60 credits): the core path covered here, taking a prompt string and returning model UUIDs.
  * Image to 3D (`mattingImage` followed by `generateModelWithImage`, 80 credits): mat an image first, then generate from the matted result to preserve a specific silhouette or concept across a batch.
  * Chibi character models (`createCuteModelsFromImages`, 30 credits): stylized cute characters from uploaded images, useful for avatars and UGC content.

All three modes reuse the same `retrieveModel` polling flow, so one integration pattern covers the entire API surface.

### A Minimal Python Example

A complete text to 3D job takes two requests: create the job, then poll until the model URL is ready. Here is the full flow in Python:
    
    `import requests
    import time
    
    API_KEY = "your_token_here"
    BASE_URL = "https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api"
    
    headers = {
        "Authorization": f"Bearer {API_KEY}",
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
    }
    
    # 1. Create the generation job
    resp = requests.post(
        f"{BASE_URL}/generateModelWithText",
        json={"prompt": "a wooden supply crate", "modelCount": 1, "disablePbr": 0},
        headers=headers,
    )
    uuid = resp.json()["uuids"][0]
    
    # 2. Poll until the model is ready
    while True:
        result = requests.post(
            f"{BASE_URL}/retrieveModel",
            json={"uuid": uuid},
            headers=headers,
        ).json()
        code_status = result.get("codeStatus")
        if code_status == 0:
            print("Model ready:", result["modelUrl"])
            break
        elif code_status == -3:
            raise RuntimeError("Generation failed: " + result.get("message", ""))
        time.sleep(10)`

The `disablePbr` flag controls textures: set it to `1` for an untextured base mesh (roughly 90 seconds) or `0` to have PBR textures generated in the same job (2 minutes or more). If you need the asset in a specific format, call `convertToFormat` with the target type.


Every asset generated by the API is watertight by design. This makes it suitable for physics simulation, voxelization, destruction systems, and direct import into Unity, Unreal Engine, or Three.js.

This emphasis on topology quality is a direct consequence of Neural4D’s underlying architecture rather than post processing tricks.

Polygon budgets separate real-time game assets from film-quality reference models. The industry splits into two tiers: film-quality generation that reaches 2 million polygons, and real-time game models capped around 20,000 polygons. The Neural4D API takes a different approach: one generation endpoint that defaults to engine-ready meshes, with UV coordinates auto-unwrapped so the downloaded .glb imports directly into Unity, Unreal Engine, or Three.js.

Output control comes through parameters rather than separate product tiers:

  * Format: `convertToFormat` exports fbx, glb, obj, stl, blend, or usdz (default glb).
  * Scale: `modelSize` sets the model size in millimeters, with any value above 1 accepted.
  * Textures: `disablePbr` toggles PBR maps; setting it to 0 generates Normal, Roughness, and Metallic maps in the same job.

Because PBR textures are generated in the same job, the output is ready for a physics-ready, material-assigned import instead of requiring a separate texturing pass.

## Workflow Pipelines

### Pipeline A: Text to 3D

  1. Request: `POST https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api/generateModelWithText`.
     * Payload: `{"prompt": "...", "modelCount": 4, "disablePbr": 0}`.
  2. Retrieve: Extract `uuids` from the response.
  3. Poll: Call `/api/retrieveModel` with the `uuid` until `codeStatus` is `0`.
  4. Download: Extract `modelUrl` and download the `.glb` asset.

### Pipeline B: Image to 3D (Strict 3-Step Process)

  1. Matting: Submit the image (JPG/PNG, <10MB, 256x256 to 6048x8064) via `multipart/form-data` to `/api/mattingImage`. Extract the `requestId`.
  2. Get Matting Result: Send the `requestId` to `/api/getMattedResult`. Extract a preferred `fileKey` from the response.
  3. Generate: Send the `fileKey` to `/api/generateModelWithImage` to start generation and receive `uuids`.
  4. Poll: Use `/api/retrieveModel` to poll status and get the `modelUrl`.

### Pipeline C: Format Conversion for Manufacturing

For physical prototyping, default exports must be converted from `.glb`.

  1. Request: `POST https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api/convertToFormat`.

### 2. Asynchronous Polling Contract

Model generation is asynchronous. You must poll for completion:

  * Query `/api/retrieveModel` using the `uuid`.
  * Check `codeStatus`:
    * `0`: Generation complete.
    * `1`: Generating (Wait and poll again).
    * `-3`: Generation failed.

## Workflow Pipelines

### Pipeline A: Text to 3D

  1. Request: `POST https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api/generateModelWithText`.
     * Payload: `{"prompt": "...", "modelCount": 4, "disablePbr": 0}`.
  2. Retrieve: Extract `uuids` from the response.
  3. Poll: Call `/api/retrieveModel` with the `uuid` until `codeStatus` is `0`.
  4. Download: Extract `modelUrl` and download the `.glb` asset.

### Pipeline B: Image to 3D (Strict 3-Step Process)

  1. Matting: Submit the image (JPG/PNG, <10MB, 256x256 to 6048x8064) via `multipart/form-data` to `/api/mattingImage`. Extract the `requestId`.
  2. Get Matting Result: Send the `requestId` to `/api/getMattedResult`. Extract a preferred `fileKey` from the response.
  3. Generate: Send the `fileKey` to `/api/generateModelWithImage` to start generation and receive `uuids`.
  4. Poll: Use `/api/retrieveModel` to poll status and get the `modelUrl`.

### Pipeline C: Format Conversion for Manufacturing

For physical prototyping, default exports must be converted from `.glb`.

  1. Request: `POST https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api/convertToFormat`.
  2. Payload: Provide the `uuid`, desired `modelType` (e.g., `stl`, `fbx`, `obj`), and `modelSize` in millimeters (must be > 1).
  3. Poll Status: Check `statusType`:
     * `0`: Complete, use `modelUrl` to download.
     * `1`: Converting (Wait and retry).
     * `-1`: Failed or bad parameters.

## External Endpoints Reference

All requests route through the base URL: `https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api`.

Action  | Endpoint  | Auth  | Purpose
--- | --- | --- | ---
Text to 3D  | `/generateModelWithText`  | Bearer Token  | Generate from text prompt
Retrieve  | `/retrieveModel`  | Bearer Token  | Poll status and get model URL
Matting  | `/mattingImage`  | Bearer Token  | Pre-process image

Image to 3D  | `/generateModelWithImage`  | Bearer Token  | Generate from matted fileKey
Convert Format  | `/convertToFormat`  | Bearer Token  | Convert to stl/fbx/obj with physical size
Job Progress  | `/queryJobProgress`  | Bearer Token  | Check percentage progress

"""One supervised creator, bounded persistent queue, no paid automatic retry."""
import asyncio
import portalocker
from ..errors import ServiceError
from .store import TaskStore

class Supervisor:
    def __init__(self, runtime, runner=None):
        self.runtime = runtime
        self.store = TaskStore(runtime.settings.rag_data_dir / 'agent-tasks.sqlite3')
        self.runner = runner
        self.wakeup = asyncio.Event()
        self.worker = None
        self.ready = False
        self.current_task = None
        self.owner_lock = None
        self.diagnostic = None

    async def start(self):
        if self.worker and not self.worker.done():
            return
        self.ready = False
        if self.owner_lock:
            self.owner_lock.release()
            self.owner_lock = None
        lock = portalocker.Lock(str(self.runtime.settings.rag_data_dir / 'agent-tasks-owner.lock'), timeout=0)
        try:
            lock.acquire()
        except portalocker.exceptions.LockException:
            # An unavailable second process must never "recover" live tasks
            # owned by the first application, even if its RAG lock also fails.
            self.diagnostic = 'AGENT_TASKS_LOCKED'
            return
        self.owner_lock = lock
        try:
            self.store.recover()
            self.worker = asyncio.create_task(self._work(), name='opera-agent-supervisor')
            self.ready = True
            self.diagnostic = None
        except BaseException:
            self.owner_lock.release()
            self.owner_lock = None
            self.worker = None
            raise

    async def close(self):
        self.ready = False
        try:
            if self.worker:
                self.worker.cancel()
                await asyncio.gather(self.worker, return_exceptions=True)
        finally:
            self.worker = None
            if self.owner_lock:
                self.owner_lock.release()
                self.owner_lock = None

    def available(self):
        if not self.ready or not self.worker or self.worker.done() or not self.runtime.settings.agent_workflow_enabled:
            return False
        if not self.runtime.search_service or not self.runtime.provider.verified:
            return False
        budget = self.runtime.provider.ledger.summary()
        scope = budget.get('activeScope')
        return budget['estimatedUpperCostCny'] < budget['budgetCny'] and (not scope or scope['estimatedUpperCostCny'] < scope['budgetCny'])

    def create(self, brief, key):
        existing = self.store.existing(key, brief)
        if existing:
            return existing
        if not self.available():
            raise ServiceError('AGENT_SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE', 'Agent服务未就绪，请检查知识库、模型验证与应用预算。', 503, True)
        task_id, created = self.store.create(brief, key, self.runtime.settings.agent_queue_limit)
        if created:
            self.wakeup.set()

+# 戏境 AI — Phase 4 数字IP与Neural4D架构方案（检查点A）
+
+- 审查日期：2026-10-11，Asia/Shanghai。
+- 项目：`D:\京剧\京剧`。
+- 状态：**检查点A方案已完成，等待用户批准开发；Phase 4尚未实现或测试。**
+- 本次范围：读取真实代码、Git与既有证据，查阅公开官方文档，只新增本方案文件。未修改功能代码、创建开发分支、安装依赖、启动服务、调用Neural4D或任何付费API。
+- 当前分支：`feature/phase3-opera-agents`。
+- 当前HEAD：`c89e63e1f5afa575b5e3972dd5cfa26a897d3942`。
+
+## 1. Phase 4目标与现有成果审查
+
+### 1.1 目标与边界
+
+将“真实文化证据 → 四Agent角色创作 → 经确认的Character JSON → 视觉Prompt → 实际概念图 → Neural4D模型 → 网页交互与用途展示”连接成可追溯的数字IP生产流程。
+
+继续保留8个静态HTML页面、原生ES Module、酒红/金色/米白视觉体系、已有RAG与Agent实现。新增数字资产模块不迁移React/Vue，不替换知识库，不扩建CRM、支付或游戏引擎。模型可供网页观察，不预先宣称已具备骨骼、动画、游戏低面数、可打印性或全部商业授权。
+
+### 1.2 用户额度要求的真实演进
+
+本轮依次收到：全部请求最多3次 → 全部请求最多8次 → **“按照实际需要进行api请求不限制次数了”**。后者是当前有效要求：**Neural4D HTTP请求不再设置3次或8次的总量硬上限**。
+
+仍按技术验证、比赛核心模型、企业展示三个既定用途规划生成工作；取消请求次数上限不自动扩大模型数量、付费预算或允许无人确认的生成。保留人工确认、幂等、请求账本、超时和查询停止条件。本次检查点A禁止实际调用的要求继续有效。
+
+### 1.3 Git与目录核对
+
+审查开始时 `git status --short` 无输出，工作区干净。`git branch -vv` 显示当前分支与本地记录的 `origin/feature/phase3-opera-agents` 同为c89e63e；本次没有fetch，因此这不是对GitHub实时状态的重新验证。main仍停留在Phase 1，既有历史未合并或压缩。
+
+真实主要结构（省略资源文件、缓存与既有测试明细）：
+
+```text
+京剧/
+├── index.html / history.html / roles.html / facial.html
+├── music.html / video.html / gallery.html / about.html
+├── css/ai-workshop.css 与既有文化页面样式
+├── js/ai-workshop/
+│   ├── contracts.js
+│   ├── services.js
+│   ├── main.js
+│   └── agent-workflow.js
+├── backend/
+│   ├── app/
+│   │   ├── agents/         # 已实现四Agent、任务持久化和确认
+│   │   ├── api/agents.py
+│   │   ├── knowledge/      # SQLite/BGE/Qdrant
+│   │   ├── providers/      # DeepSeek与金额账本
+│   │   ├── services/       # runtime/chat/search
+│   │   ├── main.py / config.py / schemas.py
+│   │   └── static_frontend.py
+│   ├── scripts/
+│   ├── tests/
+│   └── requirements.txt
+├── knowledge/ / scripts/
+├── images/ / audio/ / media/
+└── docs/{architecture,reports,prompts,evidence}/
+```
+
+没有独立的 `frontend/` 或根目录 `agents/`；不能按不存在的目录制定迁移计划。已有 `backend/scripts/download_model.py` 属于Embedding准备工具，不能因为文件名就认定具有数字角色下载功能。
+
+Phase 3八次真实提交均保留：
+
+| Commit | 实际内容 |
+|---|---|
+| `b6041be91fb26f39c002182ca45eca7b5ff772d8` | 架构批准与原需求归档 |
+| `381d62e746306d66193de1c3e62db1be25ae1b1a` | 持久化任务、队列与预算 |
+| `903fe1d94a6b927f13aca52460c30a858e2399ea` | 有文化证据的四角色协作 |
+| `81dd4516a5d42854ef488488f8aec83c24b555b0` | 工坊任务与人工确认接入 |
+| `63ce099081bc46a370e765b13de0c166fb2df2fd` | 文化断言与任务独占修复 |
+| `3d50f70f68137a19de604690bf7de5930d11a1ee` | 不确定性保留与方案校验 |
+| `d96ee0c3f29e4782675df23f16b1470a522df25e` | 需求澄清与有限实体补查 |
+| `c89e63e1f5afa575b5e3972dd5cfa26a897d3942` | 真实测试、费用与复现归档 |
+
+Phase 1基线 `04b2c571e068ec0b26205fcce0c075395caeebce`，Phase 2基线 `a95c7748e4a22bfed9f4f8261e96dffa2522b740`。Phase 3报告记载工程COMPLETE，同时写明用户检查点B待验收、文化专家复核待进行。本次核实代码和证据完整存在，没有重新执行其测试，也不把报告视为用户对每份角色方案的最终素材批准。
+
+### 1.4 Character JSON的实际适用性
+
+`backend/app/agents/schemas.py:54` 的 `CharacterDesign` 是严格版本化文字结构：姓名、定位、服饰、颜色、视觉元素、原创元素、`visualPrompt`、依据ID与限制。元素区分 `evidence_based` 与 `creative`，视觉Prompt最多320字符。严格模型拒绝额外字段，不能直接往旧设计对象塞入图片、模型或企业字段。
+
+`workflow.py`保留设计、审校、真实引用、知识库generation与Prompt版本。`store.py:170`检查四阶段完成、审校pass和无不确定性；`store.py:237`再检查确认ID和序号，完成后才能设置用户确认与允许发布。Phase 4应服务器端重读这些记录，不能相信浏览器上传JSON中的布尔值。
+
+| 已归档任务 | 实际状态 | 资产使用判断 |
+|---|---|---|
+| `0a808e2b-182e-4457-b0bb-5e4f39a66263`，青旌将·霄羽 | 已确认；旧v1 Prompt | 可作为既有文字样本，仍需本阶段视觉、图片与调用确认 |
+| `1a18ff2c-93bb-47fb-8060-3de45378a721`，蓝云 | awaiting_confirmation；Planner/Research v4、Designer/Reviewer v3 | 尚不可直接生成 |
+| `174e97bf-4df1-4970-83e0-108afc81ec73`，银翎云将 | awaiting_confirmation | 尚不可直接生成 |
+| `75783c7e-d83a-4129-8e7d-5d9482df05f9`，资料不足 | cancelled，无设计 | 禁止生成 |
+
+依据为 `docs/evidence/test-results/phase-03/browser-tasks-final.json` 和 `browser-confirmed-character.json`。已确认样本是测试过程的真实确认记录，不能据此认定用户已经选择其为最终比赛角色。
+
+Character JSON适合生成视觉指令；它不是几何、贴图、图像、骨骼或3D文件。当前视觉Prompt含“舞台写意背景”，需要另建适合图生3D的版本，保留原始文化意图并让用户审阅。
+
+### 1.5 工坊与3D能力审查
+
+`about.html:252`有概念图空态，`:260`有Neural4D面板，`:267`是未来Viewer容器；没有真实概念图或模型。全仓库源码与资源检索没有Three.js、model-viewer、Babylon、WebGL/canvas Viewer实现，也没有GLB/GLTF资产。
+
+`services.js:205/208`中的概念图与模型提交仍抛未接入提示；`contracts.js:85`将这两项能力强制归一为false。只有类型注释不代表已经具有模型服务。Phase 4需要协调前后端协议、能力校验和按钮启用。
+
+## 2. 总体技术架构
+
+推荐沿用FastAPI与SQLite，新增独立资产层、供应商适配层和局部Viewer，避免复杂微服务。
+
+```mermaid
+flowchart TD
+    A[Phase 3已确认任务] --> B[服务器核验并冻结Character快照]
+    B --> C[版本化Visual Prompt Generator]
+    C --> D[人工确认视觉Prompt]
+    D --> E[实际概念图生成或合规导入]
+    E --> F[图片检查与人工接受]
+    F --> G[生成用途与费用确认]
+    G --> H[Neural4D Service与请求账本]
+    H --> I[真实异步任务与明确状态]
+    I --> J[下载、校验、私有模型存储]
+    J --> K[受控资源API]
+    K --> L[model-viewer交互展示]
+    L --> M[个人文化体验 / 企业用途展示]
+```
+
+RAG引用、Agent版本与角色快照作为资产溯源数据，不让Agent自动触发Neural4D。问答、Agent和资产模块分别初始化；资产异常不能阻断原问答。
+
+### 2.1 Character Asset Schema设计
+
+新建外层 `CharacterAsset`，保留旧CharacterDesign原样，拟包含：
+
+| 字段组 | 拟保存内容 |
+|---|---|
+| 身份 | assetId、assetSchemaVersion、version、sourceTaskId、mode、purpose |
+| 角色快照 | characterSnapshot、reviewSnapshot、citationSnapshot、sourceResultHash |
+| 溯源 | knowledgeGeneration、promptVersions、来源/片段版本与Hash |
+| 视觉指令 | originalVisualPrompt、imagePrompt、negativePrompt、templateVersion、promptHash |
+| 图片 | imageId、hash、MIME、宽高、文件大小、来源方式、供应商/任务ID、许可说明 |
+| 确认 | 角色确认引用、视觉确认、图片接受、调用批准ID、时间与输入Hash |
+| 模型 | jobId、providerTaskId、format、size、sha256、内部存储键、校验报告、资源URL |
+| 展示 | viewerState、用途说明、限制、商业许可核查状态 |
+
+确认是三道独立门禁：**角色确认 → 视觉Prompt/概念图确认 → 本次真实生成批准**。修改图片、Prompt、源任务或用途后，旧批准失效。新资产版本不覆盖已确认快照。
+
+### 2.2 Visual Prompt Generator
+
+先采用本地确定性模板，无需新增文本模型调用。读取服饰、配色、依据与原创标签，另存模板版本和Hash，不重写Phase 3原始Prompt。技术约束包括单角色、全身完整、足部可见、构件边界清晰、简洁背景、均匀光照、适当正面或三分之四视角；禁止在画面叠加文字、水印和多人物拼贴。
+
+靠旗、雉尾、长枪、薄片与镂空结构列为高风险部件。模板不能为了成模擅自删除文化元素；需要简化时列出取舍并等待用户接受。背面细节可能由供应商推断，应记录为生成内容，不能宣称全方位扮相已由文化资料证明。
+
+### 2.3 概念图路径与外部条件
+
+目前仅有DeepSeek文本Provider，没有已配置的图像生成Provider。**不能把视觉Prompt或空态图片称作已生成概念图。**
+
+推荐先实现真实图片上传/登记与许可、内容确认，再接一个用户选定的图像Provider。上传图片可由用户在有使用权的工具中实际生成，标记 `imported_ai_image`；普通授权图片标记 `manual_image`。这两者不能被描述为本平台API生成。
+
+Neural4D官方索引也列有图片生成接口，但尚未核实该账户权限、模型、价格与完整返回协议，因此本方案不默认调用它。平台概念图API的供应商、预算、凭证和商用条件须在开发时落实；未落实则保留“导入概念图可用，平台生成未接入”。[官方能力索引](https://docs.neural4d.com/llms.txt)

+## 3. Neural4D服务设计
+
+### 3.1 官方资料核验与适配边界
+
+已阅读公开官方索引、Quickstart、模型查询说明及官方API Documentation 1.2。索引目前将3D接口放在old管理接口组，v1组主要列文件、图像与视频任务，不能把图像v1任务协议直接套到3D上。用户提供的概览属于能力介绍，不能单独决定具体请求字段。[官方索引](https://docs.neural4d.com/llms.txt)、[Quickstart](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/quickstart)
+
+管理接口示例使用 `https://alb.neural4d.com:3000/api` 与服务端Bearer Token。传统图生3D链路为：`mattingImage(image文件)` → `getMattedResult(requestId)` → `generateModelWithImage(fileKey)` → `retrieveModel(uuid)` → 下载真实模型。图片建议JPG/JPEG/PNG/WEBP、低于10MB；生成请求必须显式指定 `modelCount=1`，避免默认多个输出。生成返回UUID，查询得到真实结果URL。[官方API文档1.2，第6—10页](https://blog.neural4d.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/01/Neural4D-API-Documentation.pdf)
+
+上述旧文档可用于设计协议适配，但**不是已经验证账户当前接口可用**。部分索引中的新版图生3D页面本次抓取失败，尚未确认新字段或旧接口迁移情况。批准开发后，应先再次读取当时的完整官方接口说明，锁定请求/响应协议与版本，再进行真实请求；不得凭营销文章自行补造参数。现在没有做鉴权、余额或连通测试。
+
+### 3.2 服务职责
+
+`Neural4DService`只接收服务器登记并接受的imageId与资产版本，不接受浏览器任意外链、供应商fileKey或任意JSON。它负责参数白名单、预处理任务、提交、显式查询、响应校验与下载登记。所有出站操作经过统一Dispatcher与账本；浏览器从不持有供应商Token。
+
+拟定超时：提交/查询30秒、文件传输90秒，最终根据官方限制和实际测试调整。每次请求只有一个HTTP尝试，关闭库级自动重试与自动重定向。未知结果不自动重发生成。
+
+查询结果的 `codeStatus` 应按当前官方协议映射：成功、生成中、Token失效、任务不存在、生成失败。HTTP 200不等于生成成功，UUID不存在也不自动创建新模型。[官方Retrieve model](https://docs.neural4d.com/en/api-reference/model-management/retrieve-model)
+
+### 3.3 本地任务状态与查询
+
+资产任务状态建议为 `awaiting_image / awaiting_approval / queued / preprocessing / submitted / processing / downloading / validating / succeeded / failed / unknown / cancelled_local`。Viewer状态另行管理。
+
+- 网页刷新、查看本地任务状态、切换面板均只读本地SQLite，不隐含供应商请求。
+- 提供“查询供应商状态”操作，一次明确操作对应一次查询，建议最小间隔15秒。
+- 初始每任务20次查询或20分钟后暂停，显示最后真实状态；此为查询停止策略，不是全项目HTTP次数额度。继续查询需显式操作。
+- 不建立无限轮询、自动重新生成或Agent后台循环调用。没有真实进度时仅显示阶段与时间，不编造百分比。
+- 超时或进程退出显示“结果未知，需核对原任务”，保留UUID与历史。
+- 未发现官方已核实的Webhook签名协议；本阶段不假定可以靠回调省略查询，也不新增公网回调基础设施。

+### 3.4 文件保存与错误处理
+
+运行数据拟置于既有仓库外目录 `D:\京剧\.runtime\xijing-ai\assets\`，供应商链接用于服务端短期下载，不作为长期前端src。暂存 `.part` 文件，检查长度、内容与Hash后原子转入版本目录。

+下载URL须HTTPS、经过实际供应商域名白名单、DNS/IP与重定向目标检查，拒绝本地、内网及任意外部地址；不向下载域名转发API Authorization。供应商URL可能携带签名参数，不进入公开日志或截图。若需要额外下载请求，记录在账本中，当前没有总量硬上限。
+
+统一中文错误至少覆盖缺少配置、鉴权/权限、余额、参数、限流、服务失败、超时、未知结果、响应字段不匹配、图像预处理失败、下载失败、文件过大和GLB无效。错误响应沿用requestId，不返回Token、签名URL、私有路径或原始堆栈。

+## 6. 3D交互硬性要求及实现设计
+
+Viewer启用 `camera-controls`，支持拖拽旋转、滚轮和双指缩放。水平方位不设置有限角度限制，目标360°；垂直角度适度约束，缩放限制按模型包围盒确定，避免进入模型或缩到不可见。采用官方支持的参数形式，不把 `Infinity` 字面值填进属性。[model-viewer相机API](https://modelviewer.dev/docs/index.html)
+
+手机保留页面滚动，提供“进入模型操作/退出操作”控制；交互区域内处理单指旋转和双指缩放，区域外正常滚动。真实触摸测试要确认不会被父元素截获。设置可聚焦区域、清晰中文操作说明、放大/缩小与复位按钮，按钮键盘可用。
+
+不默认自动旋转；尊重系统减少动画。概念图在独立预览区显示，不冒充模型。只有真实几何加载成功才展示可操作Viewer；静态图片、GIF、视频不计入3D验收。
+
+至少260°的验证采用真实鼠标/触摸拖拽，同方向相机角度展开后覆盖范围须达到 `260 × π / 180 ≈ 4.538`弧度，目标达到2π。记录实际交互事件、正面/侧面/背面截图及操作录像；不能靠往返小幅拖动累计绝对角度，也不能只用程序设置相机位置声称鼠标测试通过。`camera-change`需区分真实用户来源与自动变化。
+
+## 7. 3D Viewer状态设计
+
+Viewer状态与Neural4D任务状态分开：
+
+| 状态 | 显示与行为 | 进入条件 |
+|---|---|---|
+| idle | 尚无模型，提示先选择已生成资产 | 没有获准模型 |
+| loading | “正在加载京剧数字角色模型…”；显示真实加载事件，不编造供应商进度 | 已有通过文件检查的资源，开始加载 |
+| ready | “模型加载完成”；显示旋转/缩放提示和下载入口 | 真实load/首帧完成且具有有效几何 |
+| error | “模型加载失败，请检查资源”；错误分类、返回和本地重新加载 | 404、格式/纹理、超时、模块失败或WebGL不可用 |
+
+利用真实load/progress/error事件，不把获得URL当成ready。Viewer重新加载只访问本地文件，不能隐含重新生成。源码库加载失败、GPU上下文异常和容器隐藏后恢复都要有明确提示。[官方事件说明](https://modelviewer.dev/docs/)
+
+现有 `main.js:73`以hidden切换面板，Viewer首次进入后再初始化、按可见尺寸展示；隐藏时停止无意义交互和动画，模型替换时释放旧实例。未加载、失败或下载过程中均不留无解释空白。
+
+## 8. 3D格式、文件管理与检查流程
+
+优先使用**自包含GLB 2.0**，服务正确MIME `model/gltf-binary`。GLTF兼容路径使用 `model/gltf+json`并通过受控清单提供相对资源，禁止任意远程URI、路径穿越和未登记纹理。GLB也可能含外部URI，不能仅凭扩展名认为自包含。[Khronos glTF](https://www.khronos.org/gltf/)
+
+检查流程：下载临时文件 → 文件大小/实际格式 → GLB magic/版本/声明长度/区块边界 → glTF JSON结构 → buffer/accessor/纹理/扩展检查 → Khronos Validator → 实际Viewer首帧与交互 → 人工几何/文化检查 → 发布或拒绝。[官方Validator](https://github.com/KhronosGroup/glTF-Validator)
+
+拟定初始运行保护值：图片小于10MB、模型下载上限50MB、纹理尺寸上限4096、记录实际面数；这些是拟定应用限制，需按真实生成结果与手机测试调整，不宣称是Neural4D硬限制。避免自动调用收费格式转换来“修复”文件；损坏或性能过重的文件先离线诊断与人工决定。
+
+初版不依赖Draco/KTX2压缩，减少解码器与WASM路径复杂度；若供应商实际输出必需扩展，应同源固定对应解码器并验证，不假装已支持。可离线做有记录的优化，保留原文件Hash与衍生版本。
+
+`static_frontend.py`当前不允许glb/gltf/bin/json/wasm，不能挂载整个仓库根目录来解决。新增按modelId查记录、检查展示授权的资源路由；不暴露.env、SQLite、Embedding权重或企业私有素材。现有 `.gitignore`忽略所有bin，GLTF外置buffer与测试夹具需按实际目录明确处理；正式模型和数据库不默认进入Git。保留文件长度、ETag与适合的Range支持，实际验证后才记为可用。
+
